name: one-interface-three-mechanisms
title: One Interface, Three Mechanisms
question: Can a single metabolism interface — the ports nutrients ⇒ {biomass, energy, entropy, secretions} of Fig 6 — be realized by three genuinely different mechanisms (a lumped-yield process, a saturating-kinetic process, and a real flux-balance optimization via COBRApy) while every other part of the composite, and the interface itself, stays byte-for-byte the same?
biological_summary: Fig 6 is the paper's thesis in a single figure. When a cellular description fails, the right level of description drops from the cell to its molecules — but the *interface* that couples metabolism to the rest of the cell need not change. This study realizes that one interface three ways. The coarse handler applies a lumped yield — nutrients convert to biomass at a fixed stoichiometry. The kinetic handler applies a saturating (Michaelis–Menten-like) rate, so the same nutrients build biomass more slowly. The FBA handler calls real COBRApy to solve a flux-balance optimization on a small metabolic network each step. All three conserve mass to the identical endpoint — final biomass = yield·S₀ = 5.0 — but reach it by distinct kinetic routes, exhausting the substrate at t ≈ 4.0 (first-order), 8.6 (MM knee), and 10.2 (FBA cap). All three write the identical ports; a reader can watch the mechanism change underneath a boundary that does not move.
claim: One metabolic interface can be realized by many mechanisms — a lumped yield, saturating kinetics, or a real flux-balance solver — without changing what the interface exposes.

behavior_tests.name: mass-conserved
behavior_tests.description: All three handlers converge to biomass = yield·S₀ = 5.0 and never exceed that mass-conservation cap.

pass_if.provenance: coarse/kinetic/FBA all → biomass 5.0 (= yield·S₀); mass conserved, never exceeds the cap

behavior_tests.name: distinct-kinetics
behavior_tests.description: The three mechanisms all reach the yield·S₀ endpoint but by distinct kinetic routes (substrate exhausted at t≈4.0 / 8.6 / 10.2).

pass_if.provenance: coarse/kinetic/FBA all reach yield·S₀ = 5.0 via distinct kinetics (t≈4.0 1st-order / 8.6 MM knee / 10.2 FBA cap)

behavior_tests.name: interface-preserved
behavior_tests.description: All three handlers expose the identical nutrients ⇒ biomass port set over identical wiring (law 4); the shared port carries flux in every case.

pass_if.provenance: identical nutrients ⇒ biomass interface across coarse/kinetic/FBA (law 4); the biomass port is driven to yield·S₀ in all three

behavior_tests.name: biomass-reaches-6
behavior_tests.description: Negative control / falsification: a handler that drove biomass to ≥ 6.0 would violate mass conservation (yield·S₀ = 5.0 is the hard cap). The model provably CANNOT pass this; it MUST fail, and its failure confirms the conservation bound.

pass_if.provenance: OVER-REACH control: 6.0 exceeds the yield·S₀ = 5.0 mass-conservation cap, so this MUST fail

findings.statement: Every handler conserves mass: final biomass = yield × S₀. Confirmed: coarse/kinetic/FBA all → biomass 5.0.
The three mechanisms differ in dynamical SHAPE, not just slope. Confirmed: t≈4.0 (1st-order) / 8.6 (MM knee) / 10.2 (FBA cap).
All three expose the identical port set over identical wiring. Confirmed: nutrients ⇒ biomass, one interface (law 4).

regression_compatibility.basis: All figure composites build and every executable runs to completion (scripts/build_executables.py + scripts/measure_all.py, 2026-08-16).

biological_validation.basis: Mass-conserved, distinct-kinetics, and interface-preserved pass across all three handlers; the over-reach control (biomass ≥ 6.0) correctly fails against the 5.0 cap.

explanatory_gain.basis: Swapping lumped-yield, kinetic, and real-COBRApy handlers behind one fixed interface makes mechanism-independence concrete and measurable.

conclusion:
## Claims
- One metabolism interface, three handlers (first-order, Michaelis–Menten, real COBRApy LP) as a CLOSED-LOOP batch: all converge to the SAME final biomass (yield·S₀ = 5.0, mass conserved) but with three DISTINCT kinetic signatures — substrate exhausted at t≈4.0 / 8.6 / 10.2. Same interface, conserved mass, different dynamics.

## Evidence
- **MASS-CONSERVED** — coarse/kinetic/FBA all → biomass 5.0
- **DISTINCT-KINETICS** — t≈4.0 (1st-order) / 8.6 (MM knee) / 10.2 (FBA cap)
- **INTERFACE-PRESERVED** — nutrients ⇒ biomass, one interface (law 4)
- **conservation** — all three converge to biomass = yield·S₀ = 5.0 (mass conserved); coarse/MM/FBA differ in timescale, not endpoint

## Limitations
- Toy-real metabolism: mass is conserved to yield·S₀ and the kinetic shapes are real, but the FBA network and constants are illustrative.

## Next steps
- Replace the toy FBA network with a genome-scale reconstruction to test the same interface at realistic scale.

limitations: Three mechanisms share one toy metabolic setup; the FBA handler uses a small illustrative network, not a genome-scale reconstruction.
Endpoints are fixed by the shared yield·S₀ budget, so the study tests kinetic shape and interface identity, not absolute biomass accuracy.
falsifiability: Overturned if any handler drives final biomass past the yield·S₀ = 5.0 mass-conservation cap (mass creation), or if the three mechanisms fail to expose a byte-identical nutrients ⇒ biomass port set.
